name: plinycode-dev
description: Synopsys Pliny coding agent for VS Code / Cursor — internal models only via the Pliny gateway.

walkthroughs.title: Meet PlinyCode, your new coding partner
walkthroughs.description: PlinyCode codes like a developer because it thinks like one. Here are 5 ways to put it to work:

steps.title: Start with a Goal, Not Just a Prompt
steps.description: Tell PlinyCode what you want to achieve. It plans, asks, and then codes, like a true partner.

steps.title: Let PlinyCode Learn Your Codebase
steps.description: Point PlinyCode to your project. It builds understanding to make smart, context-aware changes.

steps.title: The Right Pliny Model for Every Task
steps.description: Pick a Synopsys internal model, or let FreeAuto and BalanceAuto choose one for each step.

steps.title: Extend with Powerful Tools (MCP)
steps.description: Connect to databases, APIs, and other external tools through MCP.

steps.title: You're Always in Control
steps.description: Review PlinyCode's plans and diffs. Approve changes before they happen. No surprises.

plinycode.context.editorState.description: Tell the model what you are looking at: with each message you send, PlinyCode adds the active file, the cursor line or selected lines, and the open tabs (up to 20). File contents are not included, and the chat does not show the addition.

plinycode.context.gitSnapshot.description: Tell the model the state of the git repository when a conversation starts: the current and default branch and a short status (up to 20 entries). The snapshot is taken once per conversation and is not updated afterwards; the model runs `git log` when it needs the history.

plinycode.advisor.maxCallsPerConversatio.markdownDescription: How many times the model may ask the advisor in one conversation. Further calls are refused and the model carries on by itself. See `#plinycode.advisor.use#`.

plinycode.advisor.model.markdownDescription: The Pliny model that answers when the model asks the advisor: a concrete model id, not a router. The default is Claude Sonnet 5. The model must have a price in the PlinyCode model list, so that each call's cost can be shown. See `#plinycode.advisor.use#`.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Only in conversations that run on `auto-paid-balanced`, where paid calls are already expected.
In every conversation whose model is not the advisor model itself, including `auto-free` and the free models. **This spends money on an otherwise free conversation.**
plinycode.advisor.use.markdownDescription: When the model is given the `ask_advisor` tool, which lets a free or cheaper model ask a stronger one (`#plinycode.advisor.model#`) for advice at a hard decision instead of running the whole task on the expensive model. Each call is a paid call of a few cents: its cost is added to the conversation's cost, and it is refused once the conversation has reached its budget (`#plinycode.spending.conversationLimit#`) or its number of calls (`#plinycode.advisor.maxCallsPerConversation#`).

plinycode.compaction.threshold.markdownDescription: Where auto-condense compacts the conversation, as a share of the model's input limit: `0.9` compacts at 90%. A lower value keeps requests smaller and cheaper, a higher one keeps more of the conversation verbatim. Clicking the context bar in the task header sets it at that point. Read before every model call, so a change applies to the running conversation.

plinycode.devops.enabled.description: Run the built-in PlinyCode DevOps MCP server, which lets the agent create and update pull requests and read CI pipeline results on GitHub and Azure DevOps.

plinycode.devops.registerWithEditor.description: Also offer the PlinyCode DevOps MCP server to the editor's own AI chat: Copilot Chat agent mode in VS Code, or the agent in Cursor.

plinycode.review.beforeFinish.markdownDescription: Before a run on an auto router (`auto-free`, `auto-paid-balanced`) that changed files ends, have a second free model read the diff. Problems it is confident about go back to the working model once, to check and fix; the chat shows which model reviewed and how many problems it flagged. The review itself costs nothing. On `auto-paid-balanced`, when a paid model is answering, the round of fixes it asks for is billed like any other call; on `auto-free` nothing is billed.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Have each image described once, as text, by the cheapest model that can see images, and give the free model the description. About half a cent per image with Claude Haiku 4.5; each image is described once per conversation.

Run a turn that brings a new image on the cheapest model that can see images, image included. Every call of that turn is billed at that model's price; later turns go back to the free models, which get the image as a description.
Do not show images to the free models: they are told an image was attached but not shown. Nothing is spent.
plinycode.router.images.markdownDescription: What `auto-free` and `auto-paid-balanced` do with an image (pasted into a message, or opened by the `view_image` or `read_files` tool) when the model they route to cannot see images, which no free model can. A model that can see images always gets the image itself. Both paid options need a paid model: on `auto-free` they apply only when **Unlock Pliny paid models** is on (Settings → API configuration), and otherwise fall back to `off` with a notice in the chat. Image descriptions are checked against the conversation's budget (`#plinycode.spending.conversationLimit#`) and their cost is added to the conversation's.

enumDescriptions: The model Agent mode is set to. Executing a plan changes no model.
BalanceAuto (auto-paid-balanced): paid models for hard steps, free models for simple ones.
The model plan mode is set to, which wrote the plan.
plinycode.plan.executeWith.markdownDescription: The model the **Execute plan** button runs a plan on, so that a strong model can write the plan and a cheaper one can carry it out. The button names the model it will use, and choosing another one in its menu changes this setting. Any value other than `actModel` switches Agent mode to that model when a plan is executed.

plinycode.ci.watch.markdownDescription: Let the agent watch CI with the `watch_ci` tool: after it pushes a change, PlinyCode checks the GitHub Actions or Azure Pipelines runs in the background, without using the model, and sends the result into the conversation when they finish. Turning this off also stops the watches that are running.

plinycode.ci.board.pollSeconds.markdownDescription: How often the **CI Board** checks its pull requests and branches while it is on screen, in seconds. Unchanged pull requests cost one request per repository, so short intervals are cheap; GitHub's rate limit still applies.

plinycode.ci.board.hiddenPollSeconds.markdownDescription: How often the **CI Board** checks its pull requests and branches while it is not on screen, in seconds. It keeps checking so it can notify you when CI fails.

plinycode.ci.board.notify.markdownDescription: Show a notification when a pipeline on the **CI Board** fails or a pull request on it gets merge conflicts, with a button that runs the board's first action.

plinycode.ci.board.maxPrsPerRepo.markdownDescription: The most open pull requests the **CI Board** lists for a repository, most recently updated first.

enumDescriptions: Analyse every failing or conflicting pull request once per commit.
Analyse only when asked (Analyze in a row's menu or details).
Never analyse; the board shows the pipelines only.
plinycode.ci.board.triage.markdownDescription: How the **CI Board** triages failures: it reads the failed runs and asks a free Pliny model what failed and how serious it is. Rules on job and error text stand in when the model does not answer.

plinycode.ci.board.autoWatch.maxAttempts.markdownDescription: How many times **auto-watch** runs one action on one commit of a pull request before it stops and leaves it to you.

plinycode.ci.board.autoWatch.maxConcurre.markdownDescription: How many **auto-watch** runs go on at once, in the background. One background slot is always kept for your own tasks.

plinycode.ci.worktreeRoot.markdownDescription: Folder for the git worktrees the **CI Board** creates to work on pull requests that are not checked out. Empty puts them next to the repository, in `<repository>.worktrees`.

plinycode.worktrees.root.markdownDescription: Folder for the git worktrees of conversations started with **Run in worktree**. Each repository gets a subfolder named after it. Empty uses `#plinycode.ci.worktreeRoot#` when that is set, and otherwise puts them next to the repository, in `<repository>.worktrees`.

plinycode.worktrees.keepDays.markdownDescription: Days a worktree PlinyCode made (for a **Run in worktree** conversation or a **CI Board** run) is kept after its conversation was last active. Once a day PlinyCode removes those idle longer, and those whose conversation was deleted, but never one with uncommitted changes. `0` turns the cleanup off. **PlinyCode: Manage Worktrees** lists them all.

plinycode.trace.enabled.markdownDescription: Write a trace of every conversation to `traces/<conversation id>.jsonl` in PlinyCode's data folder (`~/.cline/data`): each model request with its messages (secrets redacted, long text cut), each reply's timing, tokens and finish reason, each tool call and result, and each routing decision on `auto-free` and `auto-paid-balanced`. A file stops at 20 MB and the folder is kept under 200 MB. Turning this off stops the writing at once.

enumDescriptions: Open PlinyCode's terminals in the terminal panel.
Open PlinyCode's terminals as tabs in the editor area, which is usually as wide as the window.
plinycode.terminal.location.markdownDescription: Where PlinyCode opens the terminals it runs commands in. Programs lay their output out to the terminal's width before the model reads it, so in a narrow panel (one docked beside the editor, for example) tables lose columns and long lines and error messages are broken up. `editor` opens them as editor tabs instead, without taking focus. Terminals of a background task stay in the panel.

plinycode.terminal.wideOutput.markdownDescription: In PowerShell terminals, run commands through a small wrapper so their output is not laid out to the terminal's width: native programs write to a pipe instead of the console, and PowerShell formats tables and errors 400 columns wide. The command still runs in the terminal, with its environment, and you can watch it. Turn this off if a program needs a real console for its output (an interactive full-screen tool, for example). Not available in PowerShell's Constrained Language mode.

plinycode.terminal.narrowWarning.description: Warn, once per window, when PlinyCode's terminal is under 80 columns wide and commands' output reaches the model broken up. Commands run through Wide Output do not trigger it.

plinycode.edits.reportNewProblems.description: After PlinyCode edits a file, tell the model which new errors the editor reports for that file, so it can fix them right away. An edit waits up to 3 seconds for the language server; when PlinyCode edits a file that is not open in a tab, as with Background Edit, the file is opened in a background tab while it is checked.

plinycode.codeIntel.enabled.description: Give the model the find_symbol, code_navigate, rename_preview and rename_symbol tools, which answer through the language servers running in this window: a file's outline, the symbols matching a name, a symbol's definition, references, callers and type, the errors in a file or the workspace, and renames across files (rename_symbol asks for approval like a file edit). Applies to the next conversation.

plinycode.webSearch.enabled.markdownDescription: Give the model the `web_search` tool, which searches the public web with the provider set in `#plinycode.webSearch.provider#` and returns titles, URLs and snippets. Queries leave your network for that provider. Applies to the next conversation.

enumDescriptions: DuckDuckGo's HTML results page. Needs no key, but it is scraped and can break or hit a bot check.
A SearXNG instance's JSON API, at the URL in plinycode.webSearch.endpoint. Recommended for teams.
The Brave Search API. Needs a subscription token (PlinyCode: Set Web Search API Key).
Google Programmable Search. Needs an API key (PlinyCode: Set Web Search API Key) and plinycode.webSearch.googleCx.
plinycode.webSearch.provider.description: Which search engine answers the web_search tool.

plinycode.webSearch.endpoint.markdownDescription: Base URL of the SearXNG instance used when `#plinycode.webSearch.provider#` is `searxng`, e.g. `https://searx.example.com`. The instance must allow the `json` output format.

plinycode.webSearch.googleCx.markdownDescription: Search engine id (`cx`) of the Google Programmable Search engine used when `#plinycode.webSearch.provider#` is `google-cse`.

plinycode.webSearch.maxResults.description: How many results a web search returns when the model does not ask for a number.

plinycode.memory.enabled.description: Load repository and personal memory into conversations and offer the save_memory tool. When off, memory files can still be edited in Settings.

plinycode.memory.maxTokens.markdownDescription: Memory budget across repository, group and personal notes. Use a token count, a percentage such as 4%, or auto (the smaller of 4000 tokens or 4% of the model window). 0 turns memory off. Important conventions are always loaded; relevant notes are retrieved for the first user message.

enumDescriptions: Propose memories after Agent edits and Plan or Ask conversations; review before saving.
Save normal proposals automatically with Undo. Important proposals still require review.
plinycode.memory.distill.description: Whether PlinyCode offers memories to save at the end of a run.

plinycode.memory.conversationSearch.description: Let the model search and read your earlier conversations (the search_conversations and read_conversation tools). The search index is built on first use and kept on this machine.

plinycode.spending.conversationLimit.markdownDescription: The budget, in US dollars, that each new conversation starts with. The task header shows a conversation's cost against its budget, and you can change one conversation's budget there. When a conversation reaches its budget, PlinyCode pauses before the next model call; send a message to continue, which raises that conversation's budget by this amount. Free models and the auto-free routers are never limited. Set to `0` for no limit.

plinycode.wait.maxMinutesPerTurn.markdownDescription: Maximum cumulative time, in minutes, that the agent may spend in `wait` calls during one turn. This does not limit other work or the whole conversation. Each `wait` call remains capped at 10 minutes. A conversation can override this in its task header. Set to `0` for no cumulative limit.

plinycode.updates.enabled.description: Automatically install new PlinyCode releases from GitHub. Checks shortly after startup and every 6 hours.

plinycode.updates.prerelease.markdownDescription: Also install PlinyCode **pre-releases** (e.g. `0.1.4-test.1`) from GitHub, for developers and testers. Leave off to get official releases only (e.g. `0.1.4`). Turning it off never downgrades: a pre-release you already have stays until a newer official release replaces it.

plinycode.updates.url.description: URL of the latest.json that describes the newest official PlinyCode release. Leave empty to use the default GitHub URL.

plinycode.memory.userShare.description: Maximum share of the memory budget for personal notes, in percent.

plinycode.memory.importantCap.description: Maximum Important entries per scope before model saves are demoted to Notes.

plinycode.memory.saveCap.description: Maximum model saves per conversation, persisted across reloads.

plinycode.memory.staleDays.description: Days without retrieval before a dated note becomes a cleanup candidate.

scripts.compile: bun run check-types && bun run lint && bun esbuild.mjs
scripts.dev: bun run protos && bun run watch
scripts.package: bun run check-types && bun run build:webview && bun run lint && bun esbuild.mjs --production
scripts.postprotos: biome format --config-path ./biome.jsonc src/shared/proto src/core/controller src/hosts/ webview-ui/src/services src/generated --write --no-errors-on-unmatched
scripts.clean:all: bun run clean:build && bun run clean:deps
scripts.check-types: bun run protos && bunx tsc --noEmit && bun run check-types:compat && cd webview-ui && bunx tsc -b --force
scripts.ci:check-all: bun run --parallel check-types lint format test:discovery
scripts.ci:build: bun run protos && bun run build:webview && bun esbuild.mjs && bun run compile-tests
scripts.pretest: bun run compile && bun run compile-tests && bun run lint
scripts.test: bun run test:unit && bun run test:integration
scripts.test:e2e: playwright install && bun run test:e2e:build && node src/test/e2e/utils/build.mjs && playwright test
scripts.test:e2e:optimal: bun run test:e2e:build && node src/test/e2e/utils/build.mjs && playwright test
scripts.dev:webview: node scripts/clean-webview-vite-cache.mjs && cd webview-ui && bun run dev
scripts.build:webview: bun run protos && cd webview-ui && bun run build
